question.text: Saraswati Growth Fund (Cat I-VCF) is winding up. The sponsor, Ms. Meera Kulkarni, holds INR 8 crore of sponsor commitment (the regulatory minimum was INR 5 crore; she invested extra). In what sequence can she withdraw her capital?

answer.text: Sponsor is the first investor in and the first to be paid out — pro rata with other LPs
Sponsor can withdraw the excess (INR 3 crore over the INR 5 crore floor) at any time; the regulatory minimum is last-out
Sponsor can withdraw pro rata after the hurdle rate is achieved, regardless of investor distributions
The ENTIRE sponsor commitment (both mandatory and voluntary excess) is locked-in and paid out only AFTER all investors have been paid in full

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the sponsor's continuing interest cannot be withdrawn and remains locked-in until distributions to investors are completed in FULL. The chapter explicitly notes sponsors are the FIRST in and LAST out, and that any amount invested above the regulatory minimum can also only be withdrawn AFTER all investors have been paid out. **The Trap:** The 'first-out' option reverses the rule. The 'excess withdrawable anytime' option is a common trap — candidates assume only the mandatory 2.5%/5cr is locked, but the PDF explicitly says excess is also subordinated. The hurdle-rate option conflates carry mechanics with capital return. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers this for all categories. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) asks LPs to confirm sponsor alignment. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) has no equivalent — PMS has no pooled sponsor concept. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When negotiating GP-LP economics, highlight this subordination to prospective LPs — it's your strongest alignment proof. In PPM disclosures, show sponsor commitment as a percentage of corpus AND in absolute INR so LPs can model GP skin-in-game vs total raise.
